description: Waycode Labs is a student-led technology team focused on software, systems engineering, AI, and space technology. We build technically grounded projects by combining programming, scientific research, and engineering.
summary:
OUTPOST is an interactive educational systems engineering simulator that lets students operate a hypothetical Mars outpost and explore how interconnected systems affect mission survival. Students make decisions involving power, battery storage, water, oxygen, food, radiation and mission constraints, then advance the simulation to observe the consequences.

Instead of learning each subsystem in isolation, OUTPOST helps students understand how a change in one system can affect the wider habitat. It combines a Python-based simulation engine with an interactive mission-control interface, educational explanations, a subsystem Coupling Map and a mission debrief.

The project also integrates real Mars radiation observations from NASA's Mars Science Laboratory Radiation Assessment Detector (MSL RAD) dataset as a reference for exploring the Martian radiation environment. OUTPOST aims to make systems engineering more accessible through experimentation, observation and learning by doing.
details:
What OUTPOST does

OUTPOST is an interactive educational simulator designed around the challenge of operating a hypothetical Mars outpost. It allows students to make operational decisions, advance mission time and observe how interconnected subsystems influence the overall mission.

The simulation includes power generation and battery storage, water, oxygen and life support, food, radiation, environmental conditions, logistics and mission constraints. Students can explore resource shortages, power trade-offs, subsystem dependencies, warnings and mission failures.

How it works

OUTPOST uses a React and TypeScript frontend connected to a Python FastAPI backend. The backend invokes an authoritative Python simulation engine that processes mission decisions, updates subsystem states, checks constraints and returns mission telemetry and events to the interface.

The educational layer includes subsystem explanations, a guided mission experience, a visual Coupling Map showing system dependencies, decision hints and a consequence-linked mission debrief.

NASA data integration

OUTPOST incorporates NASA's Mars Science Laboratory Radiation Assessment Detector (MSL RAD) Reduced Data Records (RDR) dataset from the NASA Planetary Data System. The observations are extracted and exposed through an API and displayed in the radiation reference panel. They provide real Martian radiation observations for educational exploration.

The RAD observations currently serve as reference data and do not directly drive the simulation's simplified radiation calculations. This distinction is documented to avoid presenting the model as a validated prediction of radiation exposure inside a human habitat.

Impact and creativity

OUTPOST aims to make systems engineering accessible to students through experimentation rather than isolated theoretical explanations. Its central approach is to connect engineering decisions with calculated consequences and explain why those consequences occur.

Its focus is not simply surviving on Mars, but understanding how complex systems interact, how constraints influence decisions and why a change in one subsystem can affect an entire mission.

Technology

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Simulation: Custom Python subsystem models
  • Data: NASA MSL RAD RDR dataset
  • Testing: Pytest, Ruff, TypeScript checks and production build verification

The simulation engine was tested across resource balances, battery behaviour, boundary conditions, mission transitions and multiple scenarios. The project includes documented assumptions and limitations and is intended for education, not real mission operations or flight-certified engineering.
